# Copy, paste, govern: Microsoft ghostwrote EU policy that keeps data centers’ energy use secret - AlgorithmWatch
## Copy, paste, govern: Microsoft ghostwrote EU policy that keeps data centers’ energy use secret
**The EU Commission’s policy on data centers keeps information on the energy and water use of individual centers under wraps. Research by Corporate and Europe Observatory and AlgorithmWatch, published by Investigate Europe, reveals the Commission copied and pasted an amendment suggested by Microsoft and the lobby group D...**
#### [Blog](https://algorithmwatch.org/en/blog)
#### April 17, 2026
#### [Auf Deutsch lesen](https://algorithmwatch.org/de/kopieren-einfugen-regieren-microsoft-schreibt-eu-richtlinie/)
#### [#eu](https://algorithmwatch.org/en/hashtag/eu/) [#europeancommission](https://algorithmwatch.org/en/hashtag/european-commission/) [#sustainability](https://algorithmwatch.org/en/hashtag/sustainability/)
*This text is a joint research by [Corporate Europe Observatory](https://corporateeurope.org/en) and AlgorithmWatch. The research results were also published by [Investigate Europe](https://www.investigate-europe.eu/en/).*
Since the AI Action Summit in Paris in February 2025, attended by dozens of government leaders and business executives, the European Commission is increasingly focused on ‘winning the global AI race’. Soon after the summit, it launched its [AI Continent Action Plan](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/ai-continent-action-plan), which aims to triple Europe’s data center capacity by 2030.
Fueled by the AI boom, the Commission [plans to relax permitting rules](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/dec/10/eu-proposes-exempting-ai-gigafactories-from-environmental-assessments) to make it easier for tech companies to build data centers. But their rapid expansion is already putting [immense](https://algorithmwatch.org/en/ireland-data-center-crisis-eu-sovereignty/) [pressure](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2025/apr/09/big-tech-datacentres-water) on energy and water supplies and electricity grids, and [threatens the EU’s climate goals.](https://ecostandard.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Data-centres-report.pdf)
In the Dublin area for example, data centers already consume an extraordinary [50 per cent of the electricity supply](https://archive.is/20250219024847/https:/www.independent.ie/news/data-centres-now-using-half-of-all-electricity-in-dublin-and-meath/a1415943438.html), putting immense pressure on prices and grids for the rest of society. The energy demands are so high that there are now long waiting times for connection to the grid. Therefore, big tech data centers are increasingly being powered by on-site fossil gas generators. With Big Tech companies pouring hundreds of billions of euros into AI data centers, the International Energy Agency (IEA) projects that data center electricity consumption will grow by [15 per cent per year](https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai/energy-demand-from-ai) — more than four times faster than consumption from other sectors.
The EU is trying to address this rising energy demand through the Energy Efficiency Directive (EED), which obliges tech companies to transparency on the power demand of data centers. However, new research by Corporate Europe Observatory and AlgorithmWatch shows that Microsoft played a key role in drafting a crucial article that largely makes this obligation an empty shell.
**Data centers’ energy use? None of your business**
The Energy Efficiency Directive (EED), passed in 2023 as part of the Green Deal, aims to improve energy efficiency across the EU. While the directive covers energy use across policy areas, [Article 12](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023L1791#art_12) relates specifically to data centers. It aims to create minimum transparency requirements regarding energy consumption, water usage, and the use of renewable energy. In the face of [greenwashing](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/02/18/a-milestone-achievement-in-our-journey-to-carbon-negative/) from the tech industry, increased transparency could help dispelling [baseless claims](https://www.desmog.com/2025/04/22/ai-energy-demand-can-keep-fossil-fuels-alive-tech-backers-promise-worlds-two-biggest-oil-producers/) made by companies and documenting the local impact of the global AI boom.
But while the Energy Efficiency Directive makes it clear that transparency is the standard, it leaves a crucial loophole by exempting information that is covered by trade and business secrets. A loophole that Big Tech was able to exploit.
In 2024 the EU Commission began drafting a ['Delegated Act on the rating scheme for data centers](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L_202401364&qid=1773059588135#art_5)’ to implement Article 12 of the Energy Efficiency Directive. [Microsoft](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451125_en) and the lobby organization [DigitalEurope](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451112_en) submitted position papers to the Commission. In doing so, they closely coordinated with each other to lobby for the transparency requirements set out in the EED to be significantly weakened, and for the scope of trade and business secrets to be broadened to cover all data on individual data centers. Information was only to be made available at an aggregate level. In effect, this makes it impossible to know how much energy a specific data center would use, making it significantly harder to document the real-world consequences of building more data centers and their environmental impact.
It is important to note that the vast energy requirements of data centers are creating political backlash. Resistance campaigns are increasing, from locals objecting to skyrocketing electricity bills in Ireland to communities facing water scarcity in Spain. In the United States, grassroots groups have substantially slowed down the data center rush. According to one estimate, at least $156 billion across 48 projects were blocked or stalled in 2025. While Europe is still in the early stages of the data center build out, Big Tech firms – who have staked billions on AI – have a key interest in creating roadblocks for this kind of growing opposition.
With this in mind, the reasons stated by Microsoft and DigitalEurope for blocking information on data center energy usage are deeply troubling. Microsoft warned the Commission in its [submission](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451125_en) that raw data on individual data centers could be released in response to access-to-information requests from NGOs, including those relating to the energy use of data centers.
For instance, DigitalEurope [writes](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451125_en) that “storing this data within the Commission’s database raises concerns about potential reactive data publication in response to access requests from competitors and NGOs under existing transparency frameworks”.
Microsoft pushed the Commission to go even further by restricting access not just to EU-level information, but by also making it impossible to access this data at member state level. In its [submission](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451125_en), DigitalEurope adds that confidentiality requirements in the Energy Efficiency Directive are left unclear, and that the Delegated Act should ensure that information about specific metrics is “protected” from potential disclosure.
While it is unsurprising that Big Tech companies are uneasy with the prospect of having to reveal data centers’ staggering water usage and energy consumption, the extent to which the Commission subsequently bought into these arguments is shocking.
**Microsoft, the EU Commission’s ghostwriter**
Both Microsoft and DigitalEurope proposed identical amendments to the Commission regarding changes to the Delegated Act, with the aim of classifying all information on individual data centers as confidential and preventing its disclosure – even when requested under the EU’s Access to Documents Regulation or the Aarhus Convention, which guarantees access to environmental data.
Alarmingly, the Commission simply copied and pasted these amendments into the Delegated Act. Recital 12 and Article 5.5 are essentially plagiarized from Big Tech lobbying documents – a particularly egregious and shocking example of corporate influence.
Although a Delegated Act is not supposed to contradict the legislation it implements, it appears to be the case in this situation. While the Energy Efficiency Directive aims to make all information on data centers publicly available if their consumption is larger than 500 kW, *unless* specific information falls under trade, business secrets, or confidentiality, the Delegated Act keeps *all* information on the key performance indicators of individual data centers under wraps.
In April 2026, the Commission [drafted a new Delegated Act](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/16035-Energy-efficiency-rating-scheme-for-data-centres-in-Europe_en) to further implement rules on data centers and asks for feedback. However, the Microsoft amendment is largely retained, further entrenching secrecy in the EU’s legal framework on data centers.
Problematically, Big Tech firms are also capitalizing on their win at the EU level to call for diminished transparency within member states, too. In Germany, [research](https://www.lobbycontrol.de/lobbyismus-und-klima/energieeffizienzgesetz-auffaellige-parallelen-zu-lobby-papieren-von-big-tech-124879/) from LobbyControl and Campact shows that [Microsoft](https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/informationen-und-hilfe/hinweise-zum-urheberrecht?documentUrl=/media/c8/55/506728/Stellungnahme-Gutachten-SG2503130016.pdf), [Google](https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/inhalte-der-interessenvertretung/stellungnahmengutachtensuche/SG2503310321), [Amazon](https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/inhalte-der-interessenvertretung/regelungsvorhabensuche/RV0008558/164441) and the German digital lobby organization [Bitkom](https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/inhalte-der-interessenvertretung/stellungnahmengutachtensuche/SG2507100026) (whose EU lobby office is located in the same building as DigitalEurope) have been lobbying to classify information on individual data centers as a business secret by making explicit reference to “harmonization” with the EU legislative framework.
As Big Tech companies increase their spending on lobbying and marketing in the face of mounting anger and resistance in opposition to the social and environmental costs of the AI boom, demands for transparency are multiplying. In the US for instance, Democratic senators are [demanding](https://archive.is/20260326121207/https:/www.wired.com/story/senators-demand-to-know-how-much-energy-data-centers-use/) electricity disclosures of data centers. More recently, [dozens of investors](https://archive.ph/3HkzO#selection-1480.0-1480.1) have called for site-level data on water and energy use.
The EU Commission, however, has granted Big Tech an early win: crucial information on individual data centers’ energy use and their environmental and climate impact will be kept secret – despite the underlying directive explicitly calling for their publication. As the Commission is set to put the new Delegated Act in force, the conclusion should be clear: the Commission has to redo its homework and delete the copy-pasted Microsoft amendment.

# 複製、貼上、治理：Microsoft 被指代筆歐盟政策，讓資料中心能源使用成為祕密
**歐盟執委會針對資料中心的政策，讓個別資料中心的能源與用水資訊繼續不公開。Corporate Europe Observatory 與 AlgorithmWatch 的研究揭露，執委會複製貼上了 Microsoft 與遊說團體 DigitalEurope 建議的修正文字；這項研究也由 Investigate Europe 發布。**
*本文為 [Corporate Europe Observatory](https://corporateeurope.org/en) 與 AlgorithmWatch 的共同研究。研究成果也刊登於 [Investigate Europe](https://www.investigate-europe.eu/en/)。*
自 2025 年 2 月巴黎 AI 行動峰會以來，歐盟執委會越來越聚焦於「贏得全球 AI 競賽」。那場峰會有數十位政府領袖與企業高層出席。峰會後不久，執委會推出了 [AI Continent Action Plan](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/ai-continent-action-plan)，目標是在 2030 年前讓歐洲的資料中心容量增加為三倍。
在 AI 熱潮推動下，執委會[計畫放寬許可規定](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/dec/10/eu-proposes-exempting-ai-gigafactories-from-environmental-assessments)，讓科技公司更容易興建資料中心。但資料中心的快速擴張，已經對能源、水資源供應與電網造成[巨大](https://algorithmwatch.org/en/ireland-data-center-crisis-eu-sovereignty/)[壓力](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2025/apr/09/big-tech-datacentres-water)，也[威脅歐盟的氣候目標](https://ecostandard.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Data-centres-report.pdf)。
以都柏林地區為例，資料中心已經消耗了當地驚人的[五成電力供應](https://archive.is/20250219024847/https:/www.independent.ie/news/data-centres-now-using-half-of-all-electricity-in-dublin-and-meath/a1415943438.html)，對社會其他部分的電價與電網造成龐大壓力。能源需求高到現在連接電網都要排很久。因此，大型科技公司的資料中心越來越常以現場的化石天然氣發電機供電。隨著 Big Tech 企業投入數千億歐元建置 AI 資料中心，國際能源總署（IEA）預估，資料中心用電量將以[每年 15%](https://www.iea.org/reports/energy-and-ai/energy-demand-from-ai) 的速度成長，這比其他部門用電量成長速度快上四倍以上。
歐盟試圖透過《能源效率指令》（Energy Efficiency Directive, EED）處理這股上升的能源需求；該指令要求科技公司公開資料中心的電力需求資訊。然而，Corporate Europe Observatory 與 AlgorithmWatch 的新研究顯示，Microsoft 在起草一項關鍵條文時扮演了重要角色，而該條文很大程度上讓這項義務變成空殼。
**資料中心用了多少能源？不關你的事**
《能源效率指令》（EED）於 2023 年作為 Green Deal 的一部分通過，目標是提升整個歐盟的能源效率。雖然這項指令涵蓋各政策領域的能源使用，但[第 12 條](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023L1791#art_12)特別針對資料中心。它的目標是建立能源消耗、用水量與再生能源使用的最低透明度要求。面對科技產業的[漂綠](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/02/18/a-milestone-achievement-in-our-journey-to-carbon-negative/)，提高透明度有助於拆解企業提出的[無根據主張](https://www.desmog.com/2025/04/22/ai-energy-demand-can-keep-fossil-fuels-alive-tech-backers-promise-worlds-two-biggest-oil-producers/)，並記錄全球 AI 熱潮對地方造成的影響。
但《能源效率指令》雖然明確將透明度設定為標準，卻也留下了一個關鍵漏洞：凡是受商業與營業祕密保護的資訊，可以免於公開。Big Tech 正是利用了這個漏洞。
2024 年，歐盟執委會開始起草一項「[資料中心評級制度授權法案](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L_202401364&qid=1773059588135#art_5)」，用來落實《能源效率指令》第 12 條。[Microsoft](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451125_en) 與遊說組織 [DigitalEurope](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451112_en) 向執委會提交了立場文件。在這個過程中，它們密切協調彼此的遊說策略，主張大幅削弱 EED 所設定的透明度要求，並擴大商業與營業祕密的範圍，讓其涵蓋所有個別資料中心的資料。資訊只能以彙整層級提供。實際上，這會讓外界無法知道某一座特定資料中心會使用多少能源，也大幅增加記錄更多資料中心興建後實際後果與環境影響的難度。
必須注意的是，資料中心龐大的能源需求正在引發政治反彈。反對行動正在增加，從愛爾蘭居民抗議電費暴漲，到西班牙面臨缺水的社群皆然。在美國，草根團體已經大幅拖慢資料中心的建設熱潮。根據一項估算，2025 年至少有 48 個專案、總額 1,560 億美元的投資遭到阻擋或延宕。雖然歐洲的資料中心建設仍處於早期階段，但已經押注數十億美元在 AI 上的 Big Tech 公司，顯然有強烈誘因要為這類日益壯大的反對力量設置障礙。
在這個背景下，Microsoft 與 DigitalEurope 用來阻止公開資料中心能源使用資訊的理由，格外令人不安。Microsoft 在其[提交文件](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451125_en)中警告執委會，個別資料中心的原始資料，可能會因 NGO 依資訊公開提出申請而被釋出，其中包括資料中心能源使用相關資訊。
例如，DigitalEurope [寫道](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451125_en)，「將這些資料儲存在執委會資料庫中，令人擔心在現有透明度框架下，競爭者與 NGO 提出資訊取得請求時，可能導致被動式資料公開」。
Microsoft 推動執委會走得更遠，不只限制歐盟層級資訊的取得，也讓成員國層級無法取得這些資料。DigitalEurope 在其[提交文件](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/13818-Data-centres-in-Europe-reporting-scheme/F3451125_en)中補充說，《能源效率指令》中的保密要求並不明確，而授權法案應確保特定指標的資訊受到「保護」，避免可能的揭露。
Big Tech 公司對於必須揭露資料中心驚人的用水與耗電量感到不安，並不令人意外；但令人震驚的是，執委會後來竟在多大程度上接受了這些論點。
**Microsoft，歐盟執委會的影子寫手**
Microsoft 與 DigitalEurope 都向執委會提出了內容相同的修正建議，要求修改授權法案，目的是將所有個別資料中心的資訊列為機密並阻止揭露，即使相關資訊是依歐盟《文件取得規則》或保障環境資料取得權的《奧胡斯公約》提出申請，也不例外。
令人憂心的是，執委會直接把這些修正文字複製貼上到授權法案中。第 12 點前言與第 5.5 條本質上就是從 Big Tech 的遊說文件抄來；這是企業影響力格外嚴重、也令人震驚的案例。
雖然授權法案理應不能牴觸其所落實的法律，但在這個情況下似乎正是如此。《能源效率指令》的目標，是在資料中心耗能超過 500 kW 時，將其所有資訊公開，除非特定資訊涉及商業、營業祕密或保密事項；但授權法案卻把個別資料中心關鍵績效指標的*所有*資訊都保密。
2026 年 4 月，執委會[起草了一項新的授權法案](https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/16035-Energy-efficiency-rating-scheme-for-data-centres-in-Europe_en)，進一步落實資料中心相關規則並徵求意見。然而，Microsoft 提出的修正內容大致被保留下來，使資料中心的保密安排在歐盟法律框架中更加根深柢固。
問題在於，Big Tech 公司也正在利用它們在歐盟層級取得的成果，要求成員國內部降低透明度。在德國，[LobbyControl 與 Campact 的研究](https://www.lobbycontrol.de/lobbyismus-und-klima/energieeffizienzgesetz-auffaellige-parallelen-zu-lobby-papieren-von-big-tech-124879/)顯示，[Microsoft](https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/informationen-und-hilfe/hinweise-zum-urheberrecht?documentUrl=/media/c8/55/506728/Stellungnahme-Gutachten-SG2503130016.pdf)、[Google](https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/inhalte-der-interessenvertretung/stellungnahmengutachtensuche/SG2503310321)、[Amazon](https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/inhalte-der-interessenvertretung/regelungsvorhabensuche/RV0008558/164441)，以及德國數位遊說組織 [Bitkom](https://www.lobbyregister.bundestag.de/inhalte-der-interessenvertretung/stellungnahmengutachtensuche/SG2507100026)（其歐盟遊說辦公室與 DigitalEurope 位於同一棟大樓）一直在遊說，要把個別資料中心的資訊列為商業祕密，而且明確引用與歐盟法律框架「調和」作為理由。
面對 AI 熱潮帶來的社會與環境成本，憤怒與反對聲浪逐漸升高；Big Tech 公司則增加遊說與行銷支出，要求透明的聲音也越來越多。舉例來說，在美國，民主黨參議員正[要求資料中心揭露用電量](https://archive.is/20260326121207/https:/www.wired.com/story/senators-demand-to-know-how-much-energy-data-centers-use/)。更近一步，[數十位投資人](https://archive.ph/3HkzO#selection-1480.0-1480.1)也呼籲公開場址層級的用水與能源使用資料。
然而，歐盟執委會已經讓 Big Tech 先取得一場勝利：個別資料中心能源使用，以及其環境與氣候影響的關鍵資訊將被保密，儘管作為基礎的指令明確要求公開這些資訊。隨著執委會準備讓新的授權法案生效，結論應該很清楚：執委會必須重寫作業，刪除那段複製貼上的 Microsoft 修正文字。
